title.narrative: KemI Technical Assistance to ZEMA on Pesticide Management
KemI Technical Assistance to ZEMA on Pesticide Management

description.narrative: The overall objective of the proposed collaboration is to contribute to increased institutional capacity and better practices for the management of pesticides to safeguard human health and the environment. The following outcomes are envisaged from the collaboration: 1. A revised registration process for pesticides in Zambia to support registration of efficacious products that will not cause unacceptable harm to human health and the environment is established and the capacity of ZEMA staff and other relevant institutions has increased. 2. ZEMA’s management of highly hazardous pesticides has improved. 3. An IT system for registration of pesticides is established and the information on ZEMA’s website is further developed.

Projektets övergripande mål är att minska riskerna för miljön och människors och djurs hälsa genom förbättrad användning av bekämpningsmedel i Zambia. Detta förväntas uppnås genom att den svenska Kemikalieinspektionen (KemI) stödjer den zambiska Kemikalieinspektionen "Zambia Environmental Management Agency" (ZEMA) i genomförandet av en ny kemikalielagstiftning i Zambia, främst genom kapacitetsutveckling av ZEMA, inklusive en långtidsexpert från KemI baserad i Zambia. Stödet inkluderar även utveckling av den zambiska lagstiftningen, till exempel inom interna operativa förfaranden, en samordningsmekanism mellan ansvariga ministerier / byråer / andra relevanta intressenter samt riktlinjer för genomförandet av lagstiftningen. Utbildning av personal, både registrerare och inspektörer, kommer att genomföras av KemI, som även kommer att jobba för att öka medvetenheten hos olika intressenter så som företag inom kemikaliesektorn.
Sidas avtalspartner är den svenska Kemikalieinspektionen (KemI), en central tillsynsmyndighet under Miljödepartementet med ansvar för ärenden och samordning av bland annat kemiska produkter.
Den totala budgeten för insatsen är 13,3 miljoner SEK. Projektet kommer att pågå i tre år, med start i juni 2020. Ett avtal kommer att undertecknas mellan Sida och KemI vid beslut. Avtalet är särskilt utvecklat av Sida för stöd till svenska myndigheter och har även godkänts av KemIs juridiska avdelning. Sidas kontaktperson för KemI, Thomas Alveteg, har också varit involverad i processen.

The proposed intervention aims at reducing the risks to human and animal health and the environment from the use of pesticides by supporting the implementation of new and subsidiary chemicals legislation in Zambia. This will be achieved through the development of institutional capacity of the Zambia Environmental Management Agency (ZEMA) to ensure that the population and the environment is not harmed by building a robust authorization scheme. To support this, new and amended subsidiary legislation and certain administrative tools need to be developed such as internal standard operating procedures, a coordination mechanism between responsible ministries/agencies/other relevant stakeholders and guidelines for implementation of the legislation. Training of staff, both registrars and inspectors, as well as raising awareness among various stakeholders is crucial for strengthening the institutional capacity and contributes to compliance. A long-term adviser from KemI will be placed in Zambia, with the aim to strengthen the project.
The agreement partner is the Swedish Chemicals Agency (KemI), a supervisory authority under the Swedish Government, who work to ensure that the companies' and society's chemicals control is managed in a good way.
The total budget for the proposed intervention is SEK 13,3 million. The project will run for three years, with start in June 2020. A Grant Agreement will be signed between Sida and KemI. The Grant Agreement is specifically developed by Sida for support to Swedish Authorities and has been approved by KemI’s legal department. Sida’s focal point for KemI, Thomas Alveteg, has also been involved in the process.

title.narrative: Agreement KEMI Public Institutional Support with Focus on Environment
Decision on Contribution KEMI Public Institutional Support with Focus on Environment

description.narrative:
Much of the work during the year focused on conducting a regulatory impact assessment (RIA) for the draft regulations on registration of pesticides, listing of Highly Hazardous Pesticides (HHPs and trainings related to digitalisation of the licensing process for pesticides and toxic substances in the Government Service Bus (GSB). Below is a record of activities and outputs achieved during the year according to outcomes.
Short-term objective 1: A revised registration process for pesticides in Zambia to support registration of efficacious products that will not cause unacceptable harm to human health and the environment is established and the capacity of ZEMA staff and other relevant institutions has increased.
- The Environmental Management (Amendment) Bill was presented to the Cabinet and enacted by parliament.
- Draft Environmental Management (General) Regulations on registration of pesticides and associated forms were reviewed and revised by a team of technical and legal experts.
- A regulatory impact assessment (RIA) for the draft regulations on registration of pesticides was done.
- 18 inspectors, representing all ZEMAs officers were trained on the web-based FAO pesticide registration toolkit.
- The project supported an additional ZEMA inspector to participate at the general meeting of the Southern African Pesticides Regulators Forum (SAPReF) and the associated technical training on the FAO pesticide registration toolkit and registration of biopesticides.
Short-term objective 2: ZEMA has improved its management of highly hazardous pesticides.
- A list of pesticides that appear to cause severe or irreversible effects on human health and/or the environment under local conditions of use in Zambia has been drafted.
Short-term objective 3 - An IT system for registration of pesticides is established and the information on ZEMAs website has been further developed.
- The licensing process was transferred from E-ZEMA to the Government Service Bus (GSB) where all government services can be accessed from one single website.
- User acceptance testing and training of ZEMA staff were organised on two different occasions.
- A description of the ZEMA-KEMI project has been developed and published at the ZEMA website14.
Synergies with KEMI other Sida funded projects.
KEMI strives to promote synergies between its Sida funded projects and programmes, activities and cooperations funded by other sources as well as its global work on chemicals management. Below are some of the synergies promoted.
International Training Programmes (ITP)
Three inspectors from ZEMA took part in the final session of KEMIs International Training Programme on development of strategies for national chemicals management. The participants change projects focused on Safe handling of pesticides among small scale farmers in Mpongwe District and Development of Guidelines for Classification and Labelling of pesticide to Support Pesticides Registration and Licensing in Zambia. The change projects have contributed to enhanced knowledge and understanding of safe chemicals as well as awareness among agro dealers on the importance of applying for licenses for their business.
Three inspectors from ZEMA participated in a thematic training on risk assessment and risk management of chemicals. Participants were introduced to the basic concepts of risk assessment as well as in depth presentations and practice on hazard identification, hazard characterization, exposure assessment and risk characterization for human health and the environment.
Global programme on chemicals management
In September 2023, ZEMA and KEMI took part in a physical 5-day meeting organized by SAPReF to discuss implementation of the SADC regional guidelines on pesticides management and risk reduction as well as the newly developed SADC strategy on highly hazardous pesticides. The meeting and training provided an opportunity for the ZEMA inspectors to gain additional insight into pesticide management in the SADC region, to network with colleagues from neighbouring countries as well as to gain additional knowledge on biopesticides.
